newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese firms say to chop chip investment.
newsitem.headline: Japanese firms say to chop chip investment.

text.p: Japanese electronics makers, worried by a continuing slide in memory chip prices, said on Tuesday they would cut back investment in microchip production facilities in the business year starting on April 1.

The top five Japanese chip makers -- NEC Corp, Hitachi Ltd , Toshiba Corp, Fujitsu Ltd and Mitsubishi Electric Co -- all said they expect the memory chip market to stay in the doldrums for at least another six months.
"The outlook is still cloudy," said a spokesman at Toshiba. "We may have to consider a level of investment lower than the current business year for the year starting on April 1."
A Hitachi spokesman said: "We are considering reducing investments. You can't have an optimistic view under current market conditions."
The firms would not reveal investment plans for fiscal 1997/98 but analysts predicted they would slash chip investment by 10 to 20 percent across-the-board in the next business year.
NEC, for instance, says it plans to spend 190 billion yen ($1.58 billion) on semiconductor investment this business year.

After showing a slight improvement in the Christmas season, prices of 16-megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips -- currently the mainstay computer memory chip -- sagged again in the January-March quarter.

Amid a supply glut following a worldwide slowdown in personal computer sales, some chip makers began selling 16-megabit DRAMs at around $6 on the spot market after the turn of the year, dragging down the whole market, analysts said.
Prices for volume users are being quoted at around $8 each, a level close to production costs at the biggest chip makers, compared with around $48 in early 1996.
Some analysts said, however, that the slides would stall in the middle of this year, citing the introduction of memory-hungry new personal computer models, such as MMX PCs.
"The 16-megabit DRAM market will stabilise by the middle of this year, helped by stronger demand for memories," said Akira Mimamikawa, an analyst at research firm IDC Corp.
Kiyohisa Ota, an analyst at Merrill Lynch Japan Inc, said the bearish stance of Taiwanese chip makers would also help to tighten the market after the summer.

Taiwanese chip makers TI-Acer, Mosel-Vitelic and Vanguard had initially planned to boost monthly production of 16-megabit DRAMs to a combined 30 million units by July-September, up from the current eight million, Ota said.
But they now plan to produce only 10 million to 12 million DRAMs in the period because of softening prices, Ota said.

A Toshiba spokesman said the cut by Taiwanese DRAM makers was a plus, but said Japanese makers were paying more attention to rumours about coming production cuts by South Korean makers, because of their bigger share of the global market. ($1=120 yen)
